chapters.screen: Polynomial Regression. Give a straight line extra powers of income and it can bend. Watch what happens as the degree climbs from 1 to 12: the curve chases the training districts, and the validation districts reveal when bending turns into over-fitting.
chapters.spoken: Polynomial Regression. Give a straight line extra powers of income and it can bend. Watch what happens as the degree climbs from 1 to 12: the curve chases the training districts, and the validation districts reveal when bending turns into over-fitting.

chapters.screen: Each dot is one California district: median income (x) and median house value (y). This lesson is trained on just 30 districts, one from each income band, so over-fitting is easy to see; 4,128 other districts judge it.
chapters.spoken: Each dot is one California district: median income and median house value. This lesson is trained on just 30 districts, one from each income band, so over-fitting is easy to see; 4,128 other districts judge it.

chapters.screen: Degree 1 is ordinary linear regression: one weight and an intercept. The red lines are its errors on the 30 training districts.
chapters.spoken: Degree 1 is ordinary linear regression: one weight and an intercept. The red lines are its errors on the 30 training districts.

chapters.screen: Each frame is a fresh least-squares fit with one more power of income. Training error can only fall; watch the orange validation curve on the right.
chapters.spoken: Each frame is a fresh least-squares fit with one more power of income. Training error can only fall; watch the orange validation curve on the right.

chapters.screen: Validation chose degree 3: train RMSE $61k, validation $83k. Higher degrees fit the 30 districts better but new districts worse.
chapters.spoken: Validation chose degree 3: train root mean squared error 61 thousand dollars, validation 83 thousand dollars. Higher degrees fit the 30 districts better but new districts worse.

chapters.screen: The chosen polynomial prices an unseen district: every power of its income adds a push up or down, starting from the intercept.
chapters.spoken: The chosen polynomial prices an unseen district: every power of its income adds a push up or down, starting from the intercept.

chapters.screen: Final exam: the trained model prices all 4,128 test districts it has never seen, a batch at a time. The map shows where it misses: blue = worth more than predicted.
chapters.spoken: Final exam: the trained model prices all 4,128 test districts it has never seen, a batch at a time. The map shows where it misses: blue means worth more than predicted.

chapters.screen: The polynomial of both inputs is a sheet; its degree, chosen on validation, sets how much it can curve. Same algorithm, now given house age as well as income; height is its predicted price.
chapters.spoken: The polynomial of both inputs is a sheet; its degree, chosen on validation, sets how much it can curve. Same algorithm, now given house age as well as income; height is its predicted price.

chapters.screen: Seven more inputs cut the typical error from $84k to $75k.
chapters.spoken: Seven more inputs cut the typical error from 84 thousand dollars to 75 thousand dollars.

chapters.screen: More flexibility always lowers training error. Only held-out data can tell you when the extra bends are fitting noise. Limitation: with only 30 districts the curve is fragile, and polynomials swing wildly outside the incomes they were trained on.
chapters.spoken: More flexibility always lowers training error. Only held-out data can tell you when the extra bends are fitting noise. Limitation: with only 30 districts the curve is fragile, and polynomials swing wildly outside the incomes they were trained on.
